subject: lang-dy
title: LANG.DY.------AFL.
description: Diagram in WAM-26, paired with v1-p84-1 on the same page where Braxton names language as the key vector by which western separation propagates into social-political reality. (C)LANG-DY (language dynamics) is crossed with AFL (affinity alignment): the diagram makes the case that language dynamics, in the western frame, *are* the means by which affinity alignment is constituted (and thus by which separation is institutionalized). Three radial chains expand the subject: LANG-DY → AFL → AFTD (affinity tendencies); LANG-DY → PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) → RT-INT-TR (reality initiative traits); LANG-DY → (r)POST (the reality of postulation) → PHY-U-P (physical universe particular) → INDIV-TD (individual tendencies) → SOC-RT (social reality) → EXT-FT (extended functionalism). The structural claim is striking: there is no direct edge from language dynamics to extended functionalism — the path requires passing through postulation, the physical-universe particular, individual tendencies, and social reality first. Read against the WAM-26 prose, this stages Braxton's thesis that western 'extended functionalism' (the empirical-instrumental disposition) is *produced* by language acting on postulation, not the other way around.
